idea: Signs of a hidden water leak
title: Using the Water Meter to Detect Hidden Supply Leaks
description: Educational guide demonstrating how to use a water meter's low-flow leak indicator to confirm hidden pressurized water leaks before structural damage occurs.
image_prompt: A crisp, photorealistic macro photograph of an analog brass water meter installed on a domestic supply line, vertical 9:16 format. The camera is focused sharply on the clear glass dial face, showcasing the detailed mechanical register with volumetric markings and a distinct small red low-flow leak indicator gear wheel near the center. The meter features authentic heavy brass threaded couplings connected to clean copper supply lines. Professional utility room lighting with clear directional light emphasizing the glass face and brass metal textures. Balanced vertical composition with clean background space left open in the upper and lower thirds for text layout. Physically accurate plumbing fittings, clean realistic installation, no digital text overlays, no extra graphic labels, no watermarks, no logos, no fake brand names.
visual_story: The visual directs attention directly onto the mechanical register of a standard water meter, specifically focusing on the low-flow leak indicator dial. By establishing a clear view of the physical meter face integrated into realistic supply piping, the visual grounds the lesson in basic mechanical principles: any unmetered movement when fixtures are isolated confirms continuous fluid displacement within the pressurized line.

on_image_text.explanation: If all fixtures are shut off, movement on the meter dial confirms water escaping the pressurized line.
on_image_text.takeaway: Shut the main indoor valve to determine if the leak is inside the structure or underground.
